ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Given the waveform of \( \boldsymbol{f}(\boldsymbol{t}) \) shown in the image, write the expression for \( \boldsymbol{f}(\boldsymbol{t}) \).
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the horizontal axis is t, and the vertical axis is f(t). The waveform starts from the origin at t=0, f(t)=0, and rises along a straight-line ramp to t=1, f(t)=1; after t=1, it remains horizontal, with amplitude 1. The dashed lines mark t=1 and f(t)=1. According to the usual causal signal representation, when t<0 the waveform is 0. Then reason: Therefore it can be written as a piecewise function: when t<0, f(t)=0; when 0≤t<1, f(t)=t; when t≥1, f(t)=1. Using the unit step function ε(t) to represent it, the finite ramp segment is t[ε(t)-ε(t-1)], and the constant-valued tail after t=1 is ε(t-1). Adding them gives f(t)=t[ε(t)-ε(t-1)]+ε(t-1)=tε(t)-tε(t-1)+ε(t-1)=tε(t)-(t-1)ε(t-1).

method.method_draft: Describe the waveform from the image as a piecewise function: zero for t<0, equal to t on 0≤t<1, and equal to 1 for t≥1. Express the finite ramp segment using t[ε(t)-ε(t-1)] and the constant tail using ε(t-1). Add them and algebraically simplify to obtain f(t)=tε(t)-(t-1)ε(t-1).
